name: str-eq
axis: string == in a loop: identity-equal / content-equal / early-mismatch / late-mismatch
notes: Four phases of REPS comparisons each over 64-char ASCII strings built at run time (n = total comparisons). Phase A compares the SAME object, B a distinct object with identical content, C a distinct object differing at index 0, D a distinct object differing at the last index. Rust has no source-level identity shortcut (len + memcmp), CPython and V8 both pointer-check first. Python runs REPS=750000, an 8x reduction. Measured per-phase net cost per comparison (6M comparisons, Python scaled): identity VL 2.6ns / Rust 1.8ns / deno 4.7ns; full 64-char equal VL 150ns / Rust 1.9ns / deno 11.9ns / Python 46ns. VL's identity fast path is fine; its CONTENT compare is a per-code-point loop over a UTF-32 array, so it is 12.7x slower than V8 and 3.3x slower than CPython. CORRECTED 2026-08-02 (see bench/findings/bench-strings-str-eq.md): there IS a faster VL spelling — opt.vl replaces `==` with a user-space `streq8()` whose element loop is unrolled 8x with an xor/or accumulator, and it takes the whole benchmark 2014ms -> 1259ms (phase B alone 735ms -> 344ms, 2.14x). Unrolling the compiler's own `__str_eq__` the same way (prototyped at the .wat level) does better still, 2014ms -> 927ms (2.17x), because it keeps the `ref.eq` identity fast path that user code cannot express. Filed as compiler-fixable in `emitStrEqFnCode` (compiler/emit_sections.vl:1814).

audit.startupFloor: THREE of four columns are under the 200ms floor: rust 38.3ms (18% launcher), deno 150.4ms (13%), python3 88.5ms (14%); VL 1895ms. REPS cannot be raised enough to fix this without VL exceeding ~9s. Subtract the startup baseline before quoting any ratio. measured empty-program startup on this box (min-of-5, taskset -c 2): rustc-O binary 6.8ms, deno 19.3ms, python3 12.5ms, `vl run <prebuilt.wasm>` 10.6ms.
audit.notOptimisedAway: VERIFIED not folded, two independent ways: (a) REPS/2 gives rust 1.93x, js 1.73x, py 1.75x, vl 2.26x; (b) LENGTH sensitivity — raising LEN 64->1024 (16x the bytes) moves rust 46ms->222ms (4.8x, SIMD memcmp), deno 154->531ms (3.5x), VL 1.92s->29.4s (15.3x, byte-at-a-time). Rust's 1.9ns per 64-byte compare is real, not a hoisted comparison.
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
